lista.upside: Revenue now funds LISTA buybacks and max supply was cut to 800M, so a real lending business sits under the token; today's 40% jump came with no announcement.
lista.cheap: It isn't obviously cheap: the move is led by futures (about $125M futures vs $9M spot), which usually unwinds.
lista.wrongIf: Price gives back today's jump within a week, or the December unlock of about 30M tokens lands before any news.
lista.vsScanner: Scanner reads the 40x trading spike as strength; it looks like leverage, not new buyers.

readyai.upside: Paying data-labelling customers, with 75% of API revenue routed to token buybacks; a published revenue figure would be a real driver.
readyai.cheap: Bittensor subnet tokens are out of favour and TAO has fallen six weeks running, so nobody is paying for subnet revenue yet.
readyai.wrongIf: No revenue or buyback figures published by the end of December, or price breaks its November low.
readyai.vsScanner: The 29x trading spike has no cause I could find; agree it's a real project.

byteleap.upside: GPU compute subnet with working code; the 11-23 change raising the subnet limit from 128 to 160 lowers its risk of being dropped from the network.
byteleap.cheap: Almost no coverage at all; unknown rather than mispriced.
byteleap.wrongIf: It loses its subnet slot or trading stays under about $50K a day.
byteleap.vsScanner: Scanner can't see its life signs; I found little either, so caution only.

data-universe.upside: Credible team (Macrocosmos) running a live data-scraping product and marketplace; no dated event.
data-universe.cheap: Down about 95% with the whole subnet group; no specific reason the market is missing it.
data-universe.wrongIf: Macrocosmos stops shipping updates, or price makes a new low by mid-December.
data-universe.vsScanner: The 10x trading spike has no cause I could find.

gradients.upside: Real AutoML fine-tuning marketplace from Rayon Labs; no dated catalyst.
gradients.cheap: Its share of network rewards fell from 6.7% in March to 1.3% in September, so the market is right to mark it down.
gradients.wrongIf: Reward share keeps falling or price makes a new low.
gradients.vsScanner: Scanner's 8x spike is on only about $130K a day; falling rewards are the bigger story.

hash-2.upside: Figure runs the chain and has promised a network-fee model that would make HASH pay for usage; still no date.
hash-2.cheap: Not cheap at $450M with about $50K traded a day on one exchange; it's ignored because almost nobody can trade it.
hash-2.wrongIf: No fee-model date by year end, or a token migration is confirmed.
hash-2.vsScanner: The 10.8x spike is noise on tiny volume.

sun-token.upside: SUN.io and SunPump revenue funds quarterly buybacks and burns (52nd burn about 10-27, 7.2M SUN); the next would be around late January.
sun-token.cheap: Burns are small (3.5% of supply in total), and it trades on Justin Sun news more than on revenue.
sun-token.wrongIf: The next quarterly burn is skipped or shrinks, or the HashKey listing turns out not to exist.
sun-token.vsScanner: Scanner calls it a zombie; it's alive with real revenue. Its ATH is meaningless because of the 1,000-to-1 swap in 2021.

compute-horde.upside: Real GPU compute subnet; no dated catalyst, and the 50x spike today has no cause beyond the 11-23 subnet-limit change.
compute-horde.cheap: Down 44% since first picked with the subnet group; not mispriced, just unwanted.
compute-horde.wrongIf: Trading falls back within a week and price makes a new low.
compute-horde.vsScanner: Spike unexplained; agree with nothing beyond 'real project'.

layerzero.upside: Staking opened 11-23 (staked tokens locked until 31 March 2027) and the Zero mainnet launches 11-30, both dated.
layerzero.cheap: Monthly unlocks (about 23M ZRO on 11-20) keep selling pressure on it, and it's down 42% since first picked.
layerzero.wrongIf: The Zero mainnet slips past 11-30, or the share of supply staked stays small by mid-December.
layerzero.vsScanner: Scanner flags only the trending search; the real story is the staking lock-up against the monthly unlocks.

sectorNews.AI: AI tokens fell 8-18% in the week to about 11-17 on an AI-bubble scare, then bounced slightly on 11-23 as Bitcoin recovered above $60K. TAO has fallen six weeks in a row; the one structural change was the 11-23 increase in subnet slots from 128 to 160, which adds competition for rewards. That is a headwind for small subnet tokens, which make up six of today's seven AI coins.
sectorNews.DeFi: Total value locked in DeFi fell 9% in the week to 11-20, with all 12 top chains down. Money is leaving, which hurts small DeFi tokens unless they have their own revenue story.
sectorNews.Infrastructure: No notable small-cap layer-1 news in the last week; the market is risk-off. Privacy coins (Zcash, Monero) fell about 11-12% in the week, and EU rules are pushing them off exchanges, a mild headwind for privacy chains like Beldex and Secret.
